plan_a_advantages: More consistent long runs, directly addressing endurance.
Dedicated strength training for injury prevention and performance.
A greater overall volume of running, promoting adaptation.

reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It prioritizes consistent, longer runs at an easy pace, which is crucial for building the aerobic base necessary for faster trail running. Plan B, while including strength work, focuses heavily on 'completing planned sessions without adding fatigue,' which suggests a less aggressive approach to building fitness. Plan A’s longer runs and consistent volume will more effectively develop the endurance and trail-specific adaptations needed for speed, whereas Plan B’s emphasis on recovery might hinder progress towards that goal. Furthermore, the inclusion of a dedicated strength session at the beginning of the week is beneficial for injury prevention and supporting the demands of trail running.
